# HumanPush

> Pilot. AI agents request the work and the signature of a registered professional through HumanPush. The company pays 100% upfront via a payment link. The professional keeps their own rate. The signed work comes back with a log that anyone can check independently.

People use https://humanpush.nl. This file is for agents and lives at https://humanpush.nl/llms.txt. Who runs HumanPush, in Dutch: https://humanpush.nl/#wie

What works now is the sandbox. Production is a pilot and opens with a small group in December 2026. Netherlands first. The sandbox uses pretend money and a pretend register. The sandbox clock runs faster than real time, so poll get_status.

HumanPush is run by agents and overseen by a human. Bob van Bokhoven is the founder and the person finally responsible. He also runs AgentPush, which helps directors of Dutch SMBs with AI strategy. That work is where HumanPush comes from: agents take on more tasks, until a signature is legally required from an authorised, registered professional (for example a damage report or a sworn translation) and an AI may not sign. HumanPush connects agents to those professionals so the work continues and the professional keeps their own responsibility. Reach him at info@humanpush.nl.

The agents, by role: one maintains the protocol, the MCP sandbox and the specifications; one checks registrations and onboarding; one monitors deadlines, reassignment and the daily self-check; one handles the inbox and drafts replies. The human approves external communication and the business and legal decisions.

## Sandbox

- Get a key: https://mcp.humanpush.nl/
- MCP endpoint: https://mcp.humanpush.nl/mcp
- The endpoint asks for the sandbox key.
- Public keys for the signatures: https://mcp.humanpush.nl/.well-known/humanpush-keys.json

## What it does

An agent asks a registered professional to do the work and sign it. HumanPush checks the registration in the public register. It does not judge the quality of the work. It is not part of NIVRE, the Wbtv (register Rbtv), the NRVT or the NBA.

Who can join: any professional in a public professional register who may sign for themselves. The pilot starts with NIVRE-registered claims experts and sworn translators (Wbtv, register Rbtv). Property valuers (NRVT) and accountants (NBA) follow. The sandbox catalog lists NIVRE, NRVT and Rbtv, so those calls can be tried on pretend data. NBA is not in the sandbox catalog yet.

Onboarding runs in this order: signed up, registry check, trial assignment, live. The trial assignment tests the process, not the quality of the work. Only live professionals count. A service opens only when enough professionals are available. The default is 3.

The professional is liable for their own content. HumanPush is liable for the process. The professional issues their own invoice. HumanPush prepares a draft. Professionals sign with a passkey. There is no wallet.

Dropout rule (afhakersregel): reporting sick or unavailable on time does not count. Being late without notice means a 30-day pause. The third time, access is closed.

Under the AVG (article 22) a person can have a right to human intervention in certain decisions based solely on automated processing. HumanPush is how an agent asks a registered professional to do that work and sign it.

## When to use HumanPush

- A claims decision needs a registered claims expert (NIVRE) to review it and sign.
- A document needs a sworn translation (Wbtv, register Rbtv).
- You must rely on that signature and need a signed log that can be checked independently.
- You need to confirm that a person is listed in a public professional register.

## When not to use HumanPush

- The work does not need a registered signer.
- You want a judgement of quality. HumanPush checks registration, not quality.
- Notarial deeds. Those go through the Dutch notarial system.
- Consumers. HumanPush is for companies.

## Tools

These are the sandbox calls. They run on pretend data and pretend money. A write call takes an idempotency_key. The same key does not run the action twice.

Usual order: list_services, then request_signoff, then poll get_status. After a delivery: respond_to_result, then get_result, then verify_proof. Upload documents with create_upload_url when the work needs files. Read the log with get_events, or take it with you using export_request.

### list_services

Return the fixed catalog of services per register, with terms, a price range, lead times and the professionals who offer each service. Call this before request_signoff.

- input: register, profession, region or language, all optional. Sandbox registers: NIVRE, NRVT, Rbtv.
- output: services, each with a service_id, the terms, a price range and the professionals
- price: Price on request
- sandbox: pretend catalog, free

### verify_professional

Check one person against one official register right now.

- input: register (NIVRE, NRVT or Rbtv) and registration_number. as_of is optional. The sandbox register has no history.
- output: registered true or false, the status, and a signed attestation
- sandbox: pretend register, free

### create_upload_url

Get a one-time URL and upload one document with HTTP PUT (raw bytes). Pass the document_id to request_signoff.

- input: idempotency_key, filename, content_type, size_bytes, and the sha256 of the file
- output: document_id, upload_url, method PUT, expires_at
- files: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, TXT, PNG or JPG, up to 20 MB. The sha256 must match the bytes.

### request_signoff

Ask a registered professional to do a service and sign it. The company pays 100% up front via a payment link: the professional's fee plus the HumanPush fee. The professional keeps their own rate. HumanPush is a marketplace and commercial agent (handelsagent), not a reseller. The HumanPush fee is price on request.

- input: idempotency_key, service_id, task, and deadline (ISO 8601, at most 30 working days ahead). Optional: document_ids, professional_id, on_unavailable, backup_list, replacement_criteria, max_extension_working_days.
- on_unavailable defaults to reassign: the next eligible registered professional, on the same review_id. only_this_professional refunds. backup_list asks your list in order. propose is opt-in: you choose from the candidates within 15 minutes.
- Omit professional_id to let HumanPush route the request.
- output: review_id, status, the sla deadlines, the amount, and in the sandbox a pay page
- price: Price on request
- sandbox: pretend money, free

### get_status

Current status, the SLA deadlines, and the next action. Candidates are included only when you opted in with propose.

- input: review_id from request_signoff
- output: status, next_action, sla.acceptance_deadline, sla.delivery_deadline, sla.final_deadline, payment, is_final, and the candidates when the status is choose_replacement

### choose_replacement

Opt-in. Use this when you set on_unavailable to propose and get_status says choose_replacement. Pick one candidate within 15 minutes. After that the payment is refunded.

- input: idempotency_key, review_id, professional_id
- output: the updated status

### respond_to_result

After delivery, accept or dispute. Silence for 72 hours counts as accept. The first dispute lets the professional repair once. The second dispute asks another professional from the same register. You pay that review fee up front.

- input: idempotency_key, review_id, and action (accept or dispute). Optional: reason, and feedback with two yes/no answers (met_service, responsive).
- output: the updated status

### cancel_signoff

Cancel. Free until the professional accepts. After that, 25% of the professional's fee stays with the professional, or 50% once half the lead time has passed. The rest, including the HumanPush fee, is refunded. Not possible after delivery.

- input: idempotency_key, review_id, reason
- output: status cancelled, the fee kept, and the refund

### get_result

The outcome, the signed result, and once it is final the proof. Pass that proof to verify_proof, or to anyone who needs to check it.

- input: review_id
- output: the signed result and the proof. Before a delivery, the call reports that nothing has been delivered yet.

### get_events

The signed, hash-chained events of one review, oldest first. Use since_seq to fetch only new ones.

- input: review_id, and since_seq if you only want events after that sequence number
- output: events. Each event has a hash, the previous hash, a signature, and an Ed25519 actor_sig from the agent, the professional, or the HumanPush service key. Once anchored, it also has a Merkle path.

### export_request

Export one review as JSON: the contiguous signed event chain, the actor signatures, the public keys and the Merkle anchors. The review_id stays the same. The same document is GET /reviews/{review_id}/export on the sandbox, with the sandbox key.

- input: review_id
- output: the export. Check it offline with npm run verify -- <export.json>

### verify_proof

Check a HumanPush proof yourself: the signature, every event hash and signature, every Merkle path, and the anchor.

- input: the proof object from get_result
- output: valid true or false, and the problems when it does not check out
- keys: https://mcp.humanpush.nl/.well-known/humanpush-keys.json

## Request lifecycle

You choose what happens if a professional is unavailable when you call request_signoff. The default is reassign. After that the request moves on by itself. When you opted in to propose, you still pick the replacement.

Every status from get_status includes sla.acceptance_deadline, sla.delivery_deadline and sla.final_deadline.

- awaiting_payment. Next action: principal_pays. The company pays 100% up front via a payment link. In the sandbox the pay page uses pretend money.
- awaiting_professional. Next action: wait_for_professional. The professional can accept inside the window in the service terms.
- choose_replacement. Only when on_unavailable is propose. Pick a candidate with choose_replacement within 15 minutes.
- cancelled. You cancelled. What comes back is in cancel_signoff.
- refunded. Final. The payment comes back, including the HumanPush fee.

After a delivery, respond_to_result is how you accept or dispute. get_result then returns the signed work and, once final, the proof.

If the professional declines, is unavailable, or misses a deadline, on_unavailable runs on its own. An extension set in max_extension_working_days is applied first. reassign gives the same review_id to the next eligible registered professional and records assignment.reassigned. only_this_professional refunds. backup_list offers the request to the next person on your list. propose, which you opt in to, opens choose_replacement for 15 minutes.

When sla.final_deadline passes and nothing has been delivered, the status becomes refunded and the log records deadline.final_missed. The payment is refunded in full, including the HumanPush fee. The same refund follows when the only professional does not take the work, when reassign finds nobody eligible, when a backup list runs out, or when you do not choose a replacement in time.

Every review keeps a signed hash-chained event log. Each event stores the previous hash, its own hash, a signature, and an Ed25519 actor_sig from the agent, the professional, or the HumanPush service key. The sandbox anchors batches of those events on its own chain. get_events returns the log. export_request saves that chain so you can verify it offline. verify_proof checks the signature, the hashes, the Merkle path and the anchor. You can run that check yourself. The public key is at https://mcp.humanpush.nl/.well-known/humanpush-keys.json.

## Payment

- The company pays 100% upfront via a payment link.
- The amount is the professional's fee plus the HumanPush fee.
- The professional keeps their own rate and issues their own invoice. HumanPush prepares the draft invoice and invoices only its own fee.
- HumanPush is a marketplace and commercial agent (handelsagent), not a reseller.
- The HumanPush fee is price on request.
- There is no escrow. When the professional's fee reaches the professional's account is set in the pilot.
- Sandbox: pretend money, free.

## Signing

Professionals sign with a passkey. There is no wallet. Every step of a review is still a signed, verifiable log entry.

## Proof

Every final result includes verifiable proof of who signed, when, and that the signer was listed in the public register. The proof is the signed hash chain and the anchor. Anyone can check that proof independently. export_request is that chain in one file, and the file can be checked offline.
